name: Email
useWhen: Use this for an email to a boss, coworker, teacher, or company.

sections.label: Subject line
sections.what: A short line that tells the reader what the email is about before they open it.
sections.tip: Say the topic and any date in under 10 words. No "Hi" or "Quick question."
sections.good: Lease copy needed by Friday, Nov 6

sections.label: Greeting
sections.what: The first line that says hello to the reader by name.
sections.tip: Use their name. For a boss, customer, teacher, or stranger, use "Dear" or "Hello" and their title.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.what: Why you are writing, in one or two sentences.
sections.tip: Put your main point first. The reader should know why you wrote after the first sentence.
sections.good: I'm writing to ask for a copy of my lease by Friday, Nov 6.
sections.bad: I just wanted to reach out about some stuff.

sections.label: Details
sections.what: The facts the reader needs: dates, times, places, numbers, and names.
sections.tip: Give each fact in plain words. Keep sentences short. One idea per sentence.
sections.good: My lease started on March 1, 2025. I need the copy for a car loan application due Monday, Nov 9.
sections.bad: So basically there's a lot going on and I need it for things soon.
phrases: For reference, my account number is…

sections.label: Ask
sections.what: The one action you want the reader to take next, and the date.
sections.tip: Ask for one clear action with a real date. Make it easy to say yes.
sections.good: Could you email the copy to me by Friday, Nov 6?
phrases: Please let me know by [date] if…

sections.label: Closing
sections.what: A polite thank-you and a sign-off word before your name.
sections.tip: Thank them, then use a sign-off like "Best regards," or "Thank you,".
sections.good:
Thank you for your help.

Best regards,

sections.label: Signature
sections.what: Your full name and how to reach you.
sections.tip: Your full name, then your title or phone if it helps the reader.

topics.name: General
topics.tone: Friendly and to the point. Say why you're writing up front.
dos: Put your main point in the first sentence
Use a clear subject line
Keep it under 200 words if you can
donts: Forget to say what you need

topics.name: Request
topics.tone: Polite and specific. Make it easy to say yes.
dos: Name what you need: the item, the amount, the date
Give a real deadline
Explain why it matters in one sentence
donts: Bury the ask at the bottom of a long paragraph
Ask for several unrelated things at once

purpose.tip: Say what you're asking for in the first sentence.

topics.name: Follow-up
topics.tone: Patient and helpful. Remind, don't scold.
dos: Say what you're following up on and when you first wrote
Repeat the key facts briefly
Give a new clear date
donts: Say "As I already said" or "Per my last email"
Send it the same day as the first email

purpose.tip: Name the earlier email or meeting and its date.
purpose.good: I'm following up on my Oct 28 email about the lease copy.
purpose.bad: Per my last email, I still need that thing.
phrases: I'm following up on my email from [date] about…
I wanted to check in on…

topics.name: Thank You
topics.tone: Warm and specific. Name what you're thankful for.
dos: Name what they did: the task, the day, the help
Say how it helped you
Keep it short
donts: Add a new request in the same email

purpose.tip: Say thank you and name what they did.
purpose.good: Thank you for meeting with me on Tuesday to review my resume.
phrases: I appreciate you taking the time to…

ask.what: An optional next step, or a simple offer to return the favor.
ask.tip: You don't need to ask for anything. An offer to help back or a plan to stay in touch works.
ask.good: Please let me know if I can return the favor.
ask.bad: Anyway can u also send me that other file
phrases: Please let me know if I can return the favor.
I'll keep you posted on how it goes.
I look forward to working with you again.

topics.name: Asking a Teacher/Instructor
topics.tone: Respectful and prepared. Show you've tried first.
dos: Use their title (Professor, Dr., Mr., Ms.)
Name your class and section
Say what you already tried
donts: Ask something the syllabus already answers

purpose.tip: Name your class, section, and the question in the first two sentences.
purpose.good: I'm in your English 101 class, section 4, and I have a question about the essay due Nov 12.
purpose.bad: i have a question about the thing

topics.name: Calling Out Sick
topics.tone: Short and responsible. No need for medical details.
dos: Say which day(s) you'll be out
Say who is covering or what's handed off
Say when you'll check in
donts: Send it after your shift starts

purpose.tip: Say you're sick and which day you'll be out.
purpose.good: I'm sick and won't be able to work my shift on Wednesday, Oct 28.
purpose.bad: I feel super gross so im not coming in
phrases: I'm sick and can't work my shift on [date].
I need to take a sick day on [date].

details.what: What's handed off and who can cover.
details.tip: List any work due that day and who can handle it.
details.good: Dana has the Smith order, and the 2 p.m. call can move to Thursday.

topics.name: Meeting Request
topics.tone: Clear and flexible. Make it easy to pick a time.
dos: Say what the meeting is for
Offer two or three exact times
Say how long it will take and where
donts: Forget the time zone if it matters

ask.tip: Offer two or three exact times and ask which works.
ask.good: Are you free Tuesday, Nov 3 at 10 a.m. or Wednesday, Nov 4 at 2 p.m. for 30 minutes?
phrases: Would [day, date] at [time] work for you?
The meeting will take about [length] in [place].

topics.name: Reply
topics.tone: Clear and helpful. Answer first, then add anything else.
dos: Answer their question in your first sentence
Answer every question they asked
Say what happens next
donts: Repeat their whole email back to them
Make them read to the end for the answer

subject.tip: Keep their subject line, so the reader can find the whole conversation.
subject.good: Re: Lease copy needed by Friday, Nov 6

purpose.tip: Give the answer first. The reader asked, so that's what they want.
purpose.good: Yes, I can send the lease copy by Friday, Nov 6.
purpose.bad: Thanks for your email, I got it and I'm going to look into things.
phrases: Thank you for asking about [topic]. The answer is…
Here is the [item] you asked for.

details.tip: Answer each of their other questions. A short numbered list works well for more than two.
details.good: The copy will come from our office on Thursday, Nov 5. It covers all 12 months of your lease.
details.bad: Please see below for everything regarding the matter.

topics.name: Saying No
topics.tone: Kind and firm. Say no once, then offer what you can.
dos: Thank them for asking
Say no in one plain sentence
Give one honest reason, if you can
Offer another way to help
donts: Hide the no inside a long story

purpose.tip: Thank them, then say no in plain words. Don't make the reader guess.
purpose.good: Thank you for inviting me to lead the Nov 12 training. I can't take it on.
purpose.bad: So sorry, this is super tough, maybe I could possibly try but probably not.
phrases: Thank you for thinking of me. I can't…
Thank you for asking. This time I have to say no.
I appreciate the offer, and I won't be able to…

details.tip: Give one honest reason. You don't owe the reader a long story.
details.good: My team's report is due Nov 13, and it needs all my time until then.
details.bad: Well, there are so many things going on right now, you know how it is.

ask.tip: Offer what you can do, or who else could help. If there's nothing to offer, wish them well.
ask.good: Would Ms. Lee be a good fit? I can also help in December.
phrases: I can help with [smaller thing] instead.

topics.name: Introducing Yourself
topics.tone: Warm and brief. Say who you are and why you're writing.
dos: Say who you are in your first sentence
Say who sent you or how you found them
Ask for one small next step
donts: Ask for a big favor right away
Send the same email to everyone

subject.tip: Say who sent you or what you're writing about, so a stranger will open it.
subject.good: Mr. Lee suggested I contact you about the intern opening

purpose.tip: Say your name, what you do, and why you're writing to this person.
purpose.good: My name is Ana Ruiz, and Mr. Lee suggested I write to you about the intern opening.
purpose.bad: You don't know me, but I've always wanted to do something like this.
phrases: My name is [name], and I'm a [role] at [place].
[Name] suggested I write to you about…
I found your name on [place], and I'm writing about…

details.tip: Give one or two facts that show why you're worth a reply. Save the rest.
details.good: I finished the office skills program at Valley College in May, and I've run the front desk at the clinic since June.
details.bad: I was born in 1999 and always liked computers, and after high school I tried several things.

ask.tip: Ask for one small step the reader can say yes to.
ask.good: Could we talk for 15 minutes by Friday, Nov 6?
phrases: Could we talk for [minutes] minutes on [day]?
May I send you my resume?
